validity.researcher_notes:
P8038 has no gem.wiki page (confirmed absent from wiki_citations.json, which only covers P8000/P8002 in this scope) — this is open-web/primary-document research from scratch, per the scope note.

The row's only current ref for every field (Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Length/Diameter/Location) is the EGAS Annual Report 2018 PDF. I fetched the full 22MB PDF and ran pdftotext over all 36 pages: the strings 'Ras Bakr', 'Sokhna' and 'Za'frana' do NOT occur anywhere in the extracted text, and the existing_ref_checks' 'content present' PASS for Length/Diameter is a false positive — it is just matching the bare digits '192' and '16' occurring elsewhere in 36 pages of unrelated text/page numbers, not text about this pipeline. Per the scope's own rule ('a report cited for a pipeline is not unsupported until its MAPS have been read, not just its text'), I rendered the PDF page carrying the printed page number '35' (PDF page 19 — confirmed by the '35' footer visible in the extracted text) at 400 dpi and read it directly. That page is GASCO's 'Natural Gas National Grid' map (the same map the scope guidance describes NA using to identify this whole 40-row cohort).

On the map, a green line (green = 'EXISTING P/L' per the map's own legend, as opposed to red 'UNDER CONS. P/L' or blue 'UNDER STUDY. P/L') runs south from the Ain Sokhna/Suez hub along the Gulf of Suez coast, past a place labelled 'Za'frana', to a red facility icon labelled 'Ras Bakr' / 'Unit 103 Gupco'. Two distance callouts are stacked on this exact stretch of pipe, both leader-lined to the same corridor just above the Ras Bakr icon: '16" 192 k.m' and '16" 256 k.m'. The '16" 192 k.m' callout is an EXACT match, digit for digit, to P8038's current LengthKnown (192.00 km) and Diameter (16 in) — this is independent visual confirmation of both spec values straight from the primary source EGAS/GASCO document, and it also confirms the pipeline physically EXISTS (it is drawn as 'existing', not a proposed/under-study line) and supports Status=operating (the map has no literal word 'operating' to full-text-match — that column's automated check correctly reported no textual hit — but the green line color is GASCO's own visual encoding of the same fact).

Duplicate check against the roster: the adjacent '16" 256 k.m' callout on the SAME corridor is an exact match for roster row P8016 ('Ras Shukheir-Suez Trunkline Gas Pipeline', 256 km, 16"), whose line continues south past Ras Bakr and Ras Ghareb to a separate 'Ras Shukeir' facility further down the coast (itself labelled with its own distinct '16" 75 k.m' Ras Ghareb->Ras Shukeir callout: 256-192=64 km, in the right ballpark for the remaining Ras Bakr->Ras Shukeir leg once coastal routing slack is allowed for, vs. the map's directly-labelled 75 km for the shorter Ras Ghareb->Ras Shukeir sub-leg -- self-consistent, not exact, as expected for two independently-drawn callouts). So P8038 and P8016 are two different named GASCO assets sharing one drawn corridor and both terminate at different, named facilities (Ras Bakr vs. Ras Shukeir) with different lengths — this is the 'two real parallel/successive lines' case, not the 'same name + same diameter + same length' duplicate signature. Not flagging as a duplicate or recommending a merge.

Classification: drawn on GASCO's NATURAL GAS grid map specifically (not an oil/products map), consistent with Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission; it feeds a GUPCO Gulf-of-Suez oil-production facility (Ras Bakr, 'Unit 103 Gupco') from the Ain Sokhna hub, a plausible gas-fuel supply trunk to oilfield operations rather than a misclassified crude/products line.

Location: StartLocation 'Ras bakr' / StartState-Province 'Red Sea' and End 'Ain Sokhna' / 'Suez' match the real geography — Ras Bakr and Ras Ghareb sit in Red Sea Governorate just south of the Suez/Ain Sokhna coastal strip; no country/province concern.

Caveat (why this is 'confirmed (caveat)' and not a clean 'confirmed'): this remains SINGLE-sourced. I looked for a second independent source (GUPCO, EGPC/EGAS press material, industry press covering this specific Ras Bakr spur) but this session's WebSearch tool had already exhausted its 200/200 call budget from earlier work in this run before I reached P8038, and WebFetch fallbacks against DuckDuckGo/Bing/Ecosia either hit a CAPTCHA wall or returned generic unrelated results (no real search capability without a JS-executing search engine). So tier is MEDIUM: one strong, official, primary-source document (EGAS's own audited annual report map), visually read and matching exactly, but not corroborated by a second independent source. Capacity is left unfilled — the GASCO map carries diameter and length only, no throughput figure, and no other source was found for it; per instructions I am not fabricating a number for a weak/unsourced field.
